audit_findings.title: FY2025 OE contains only partial-year interest on the current debt claim
audit_findings.magnitude: unquantified net; H1 2026 net interest of $53.259m annualizes to $106.518m, $26.368m above FY2025's $80.150m
audit_findings.mechanism: A full-year financing-cost normalization would reduce anchor OE and every projected year, including terminal value; annualizing the financed acquisition's operating contribution could partly offset it.
audit_findings.evidence: The increase is primarily due to $32.0 million of higher interest expense on a greater outstanding balance of senior notes resulting from the issuance of the 2033 Senior Notes (as defined below) and the 2030 Senior Notes (as defined below) during 2025, partially offset by the impact of the repayment of the 2026 Senior Notes in March 2025.
audit_findings.explanation: The partial-year interest mismatch is demonstrated, but the net correction is unresolved because the acquired operations also contributed for only part of FY2025. The interest-only difference is large enough to move the $147.11 base value below the $146.39 market price; using the computed $26.368m proxy would reduce base value by about $370.4m or $6.66 per share before any operating offset.
audit_findings.action: Recast FY2025 OE with the full-year coupons, commitment fees and financing-cost amortization applicable to the June 2026 debt structure, separately annualize the acquired assets' operating contribution and rerun all scenarios using the net normalization.

audit_findings.title: The bridge may treat operating liquidity as excess cash
audit_findings.magnitude: up to $611.568m, or $10.99 per share; June 2026 current assets excluding cash were $1,543.503m versus $1,764.668m of current liabilities
audit_findings.mechanism: Any cash required for operations or near-term liabilities should not be added as a separate non-operating asset in the equity bridge.
audit_findings.evidence: As of December 31, 2025, we had $2,156.7 million of liquidity available, including $1,967.2 million of aggregate unused borrowing base capacity available under our Credit Facility (as defined below) and $189.5 million in cash and cash equivalents.
audit_findings.explanation: Adding all cash is demonstrated, but the amount that is genuinely excess is unresolved. The maximum exposure is material: removing the entire balance would reduce base value from $147.11 to approximately $136.12 per share. Current liabilities also exceeded noncash current assets by $221.165m, reinforcing the need for an operating-cash analysis without proving that this full amount must be retained.
audit_findings.action: Reconcile the June 2026 cash balance against unrestricted status, normal working capital, accrued capital expenditures, taxes, dividends and other near-term obligations; rerun the bridge using only demonstrably excess cash.

audit_findings.title: ARO cash burden may exceed the amount represented by current OE
audit_findings.magnitude: unquantified adjustment; filed ARO was $482.707m at 2026-06-30, including $50.677m current, after a $147.079m FY2025 upward revision
audit_findings.mechanism: Plugging and abandonment settlements must enter OE through sustaining expenditures or otherwise be recognized as a senior claim; omitting future cash settlements overstates operating value.
audit_findings.evidence: The revisions to estimates included in the table above increased the ARO liability by $ 147.1 million, which was primarily comprised of $ 98.7 million related to updates in the plugging and abandonment cost estimates of the Company’s wells in North Dakota and $ 48.4 million related to lower estimated well lives as a result of decreased oil and gas prices.
audit_findings.explanation: The obligation and revision are demonstrated, but omission from OE is not: the record does not show whether sustaining capex already covers forecast abandonment spending. The $482.707m liability equals about $8.68 per diluted share, so a substantial uncovered portion could change the valuation conclusion.
audit_findings.action: Map historical and forecast ARO settlements by year to the sustaining-capex deductions embedded in OE, including inflation and accelerated retirement assumptions, then rerun the DCF for any uncovered cash burden without double counting amounts already included.

audit_findings.title: Temporary derivative gains may have been capitalized as durable earnings
audit_findings.magnitude: up to $125.4m of FY2025 commodity derivative gain, comprising $61.6m unrealized and $63.8m realized; exact retained amount unquantified
audit_findings.mechanism: Any retained mark-to-market gain or nonrecurring hedge settlement inflates anchor OE and is compounded through growth and terminal value.
audit_findings.evidence: The net gain of $125.4 million on commodity derivative contracts included a realized gain of $63.8 million on settled commodity derivative contracts, coupled with an unrealized gain of $61.6 million related to the change in fair value of our commodity derivative contracts primarily driven by a downward shift in the futures curve for forecasted commodity prices.
audit_findings.explanation: The gains are demonstrated, but their inclusion in the $529.1m anchor is unresolved. If the full $125.4m were retained, it would equal 23.7% of anchor OE and imply roughly $1.762bn or $31.67 per share of base-case operating value, making the exposure clearly capable of changing the conclusion. The unrealized and realized components require different normalization treatment.
audit_findings.action: Reconcile the OE calculation line by line to the derivative gain and cash-settlement entries; remove unrealized fair-value changes and normalize realized settlements to the scenario commodity prices and the finite 2026-2028 hedge schedule, then rerun all scenarios.

audit_findings.title: Declining production could expose unmodeled deficiency payments
audit_findings.magnitude: unquantified; $553.281m of estimable June 2026 volume commitments excludes possible deficiency payments
audit_findings.mechanism: If forecast production falls below contractual minimums, deficiency payments or third-party purchases would reduce future OE, particularly under declining-production paths.
audit_findings.evidence: The table above does not include any such deficiency payments that may be incurred under the Company’s physical delivery contracts, since it cannot be predicted with accuracy the amount and timing of any such penalties incurred.
audit_findings.explanation: This is a forward-looking contractual exposure rather than a demonstrated error in current OE. The filed commitment total establishes scale but is not the deficiency loss: management states that the amount and timing of penalties cannot be predicted, and production or purchased volumes may satisfy the commitments.
audit_findings.action: Build a contract-by-contract minimum-volume schedule and compare it with basin-level production under each valuation scenario; include modeled deficiency payments or purchase-margin losses whenever forecast volumes do not cover commitments and update the monitor each quarter.

audit_findings.title: A non-recurring production-tax refund may remain in the anchor
audit_findings.magnitude: $20.9m, equal to 4.0% of the $529.1m anchor; if fully retained, computed base-value exposure is approximately $293.6m or $5.28 per share
audit_findings.mechanism: A one-time tax refund retained in anchor OE would be grown and capitalized through the explicit forecast and terminal value.
audit_findings.evidence: Excluding the $46.0 million increase in production taxes attributable to our expanded operations after the Arrangement, production taxes decreased $66.6 million primarily due to a decrease in crude oil revenues year over year due to lower crude oil realized prices and decreased $20.9 million as a result of a reduction in the production tax rate during the year ended December 31, 2025 primarily due to a non-recurring refund related to certain North Dakota wells receiving an extraction tax exemption.
audit_findings.explanation: The non-recurring $20.9m refund is demonstrated, but its retention in OE is unresolved. Despite its low audit severity, the computed sensitivity exceeds the $0.72 per-share gap between base value and market price, so it is capable of changing the valuation conclusion.
audit_findings.action: Trace the refund through production-tax expense, operating cash flow and the OE adjustments; remove any retained nonrecurring benefit, apply the continuing production-tax burden and rerun all scenarios.
